q: Which RAID level mirrors data across two drives and tolerates one drive failure?

q: RAID 5 requires a minimum of how many drives?

q: A user needs fast storage for video scratch disks and chooses RAID 0. The PRIMARY risk is
options: Losing all data if any single drive fails
Half the capacity of one drive

q: DDR4 modules cannot be installed in DDR5 slots primarily because

q: Installing two identical RAM sticks in the paired slots on a motherboard enables

q: ECC memory is MOST appropriate for

A server that must detect and correct single-bit errors
explain: ECC RAM detects and corrects single-bit errors, which matters for servers and workstations that cannot tolerate silent corruption.

q: A CPU begins thermal throttling under load. The FIRST thing to verify is
options: The heatsink is fully seated with proper thermal paste coverage
explain: Poor heatsink contact or dried/missing thermal paste is the most common cause of sudden thermal throttling.

q: Which cooler type is required when a CPU has a very high TDP and the case has room for a radiator?

q: An NVMe M.2 drive is significantly faster than a SATA SSD mainly because

q: Which M.2 form factor is standard in most desktop motherboards and laptops?
explain: 2280 (22mm wide, 80mm long) is the most common M.2 SSD size for desktops and laptops.

q: A technician needs to add a second NVMe drive but the board has one M.2 slot. A workable option is
options: A PCIe x4 adapter card with an M.2 slot
explain: PCIe adapter cards host an M.2 NVMe drive and connect it to the PCIe bus at full speed.

q: Which panel type generally offers the best color accuracy and viewing angles for design work?
explain: IPS panels are preferred for color-critical work due to wide viewing angles and consistent color.

q: A gamer prioritizing the fastest response time and highest refresh rates would typically choose
options: A TN or fast-IPS gaming monitor
explain: Gaming monitors use TN or fast-IPS panels rated at 144Hz+ with low response times.

q: OLED displays differ from LCDs mainly because
options: Each pixel emits its own light, enabling true blacks
explain: OLED pixels are self-emissive, so black pixels are fully off, producing perfect contrast.

q: A docking station connects a laptop to external monitors and peripherals typically through
options: A single USB-C or Thunderbolt cable
explain: Modern docks use one USB-C/Thunderbolt connection carrying video, data, and power delivery.

q: Which USB-C feature lets the port carry a native DisplayPort video signal?
explain: DisplayPort Alt Mode routes DP signals over USB-C pins, enabling monitors without adapters converting protocols.

q: A scanner with an ADF is chosen when the office needs to
explain: An Automatic Document Feeder feeds stacks of pages through the scanner unattended.

q: Which printer type is BEST for multi-part carbon-copy invoices at a warehouse counter?
explain: Impact printers physically strike the ribbon, marking all copies of multi-part forms at once.

q: A retail receipt printer is almost always which type?
explain: Direct thermal printers are fast, quiet, and ink-free, making them standard for receipts.

q: A 3D printer fails to stick the first layer to the bed. The MOST likely fix is
options: Replace the filament with a different color
Re-level the bed and clean its surface
explain: Poor first-layer adhesion is usually bed leveling or contamination; a clean, level bed fixes most cases.

q: Which filament is the easiest and most common choice for general-purpose 3D printing?
explain: PLA prints at low temperatures with minimal warping, making it the default general-purpose filament.

q: A barcode scanner at a warehouse must read damaged labels from a distance. The best choice is
options: A laser or imager-based long-range scanner
explain: Long-range laser/imager scanners read poor-quality codes from meters away; pen wands need contact swipes.

q: A surge protector differs from a UPS in that a surge protector
options: Offers no battery backup during an outage
explain: Surge protectors only clamp voltage spikes; a UPS adds battery runtime and often conditioning.

q: When sizing a UPS for a workstation, the two key ratings to match are
explain: The UPS must supply the load's watts (within its VA rating) for the desired number of minutes.

q: A technician testing whether a PSU outputs standby power would use

explain: The +5VSB rail supplies standby power; a tester or multimeter verifies it before deeper diagnosis.

q: Which connector supplies supplemental power directly to a high-end GPU?

q: Which storage interface is hot-swappable in a typical server drive bay design?
options: SAS/SATA drives in a backplane with trays
explain: Server bays use trays on a backplane so SAS/SATA drives can be replaced without powering down.

q: A NAS differs from direct-attached storage because a NAS
options: Plugs into one PC by USB only
Connects to clients over the network as a file server
explain: A NAS is a dedicated network file server; DAS attaches directly to a single host.

q: An SD card marked UHS-I U3 guarantees a minimum sustained write speed of
explain: The U3 speed class guarantees at least 30 MB/s sustained writes, suitable for 4K video recording.

q: A user complains a new 4K monitor only runs at 30Hz over HDMI. The likely cause is

explain: HDMI 1.4 supports 4K only at 30Hz; HDMI 2.0 or DisplayPort is needed for 4K60.

q: Which adapter situation requires an ACTIVE converter rather than a passive adapter?
options: Converting a digital HDMI signal to analog VGA
HDMI to DisplayPort alt-mode on USB-C
explain: Digital-to-analog conversion needs active electronics; passive adapters only work when signals are electrically compatible.

q: A biometric fingerprint reader on a laptop fails to recognize any finger but Windows loads fine. Best first step is
options: Clean the sensor and re-enroll the fingerprints
explain: Contaminated sensors and worn enrollments are the common causes; clean and re-enroll before hardware replacement.

q: A webcam shows a black image in every app on a new laptop. A privacy feature to check FIRST is
options: The physical privacy shutter or camera kill switch
explain: Many laptops ship with a sliding privacy shutter or Fn-key camera disable that blocks video in all apps.

q: A technician needs to crimp a custom-length patch cable. The tools required are
options: A punchdown tool and a 110 block
A crimper, RJ45 connectors, and a cable tester to verify
A soldering iron and heat gun
explain: Field-terminated patch cables are crimped with RJ45 plugs and then verified with a cable tester.

q: Which device extends a single HDMI run well beyond the normal cable length limit?
options: A passive coupler joining two cables
explain: HDBaseT extenders carry HDMI over network cabling for tens of meters without signal loss.

q: A user wants one cable from a laptop to drive two external monitors and charge. The requirement is
options: A Thunderbolt dock with power delivery
explain: A Thunderbolt dock provides multi-monitor output, peripherals, and laptop charging over one cable.

q: A graphics workstation's GPU is bottlenecked by an older CPU during rendering previews. This imbalance is BEST described as
options: The CPU cannot feed work to the GPU fast enough
explain: When the CPU cannot prepare frames/tasks as fast as the GPU can process them, GPU utilization drops; upgrading the weaker link restores balance.

q: A host with an IP address of 169.254.10.5 and no gateway most likely

Failed to reach a DHCP server and self-assigned an APIPA address
explain: 169.254.x.x is APIPA: Windows assigns it when DHCP offers are not received, limiting the host to local-segment traffic.

q: The DHCP lease process follows which order?
explain: DORA: the client Discovers, servers Offer, the client Requests, and the server Acknowledges the lease.

q: A DHCP relay agent (IP helper) is needed when

The server runs out of addresses
DNS is handled by another server

q: Which DNS record maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
explain: AAAA records hold IPv6 addresses; A records hold IPv4 addresses.

q: Which DNS record directs email for a domain to its mail servers?
explain: MX (Mail Exchange) records list the mail servers for a domain, with priority values.

q: A PTR record is used for

explain: PTR records in reverse zones map IPs to names, used by logging and mail validation.

q: A TXT record containing SPF data helps receiving mail servers

explain: SPF in a TXT record lists authorized sending hosts so receivers can spot spoofed senders.

q: FTP uses which ports for control and data in its classic form?

explain: FTP separates a control channel on 21 from data transfers, classically on port 20 in active mode.

q: SNMP managers poll agents and receive traps on which ports?

q: A /24 subnet provides how many usable host addresses?

q: Which address is the loopback for IPv6?

q: Latency, bandwidth, and jitter: which one describes variation in packet arrival times?

q: QoS on a network is primarily used to

q: 802.3at (PoE+) supplies up to how much power per port?

q: A PoE injector is used when

A non-PoE switch must power a device such as an access point

q: Jumbo frames increase the standard Ethernet MTU from 1,500 bytes to about

q: Which fiber type supports the longest distances?

q: A PUK code is required when

q: Push email differs from fetch email in that push

q: A phone's hotspot works for a laptop but a tablet on the same hotspot gets no internet. A likely cause is

The tablet's MAC address is randomized

q: Which tethering method typically gives the most stable connection and charges the phone at the same time?

q: A Qi wireless charger is slow and the phone gets warm. The FIRST thing to check is
options: The charger is plugged into a low-power USB port

Alignment of the phone's coil with the charger pad
The phone case is too thick
explain: Misaligned coils waste energy as heat and slow charging; centering the phone and removing thick cases helps.

q: USB Power Delivery fast charging requires

explain: USB-PD negotiates higher voltage/current; both the charger and cable must support the negotiated wattage.

q: AirPrint and Android printing services let a phone print by

Pairing the phone to the printer over Bluetooth only
Using the phone's USB port only
Saving the document to a USB drive first

q: A user's smartwatch stops syncing after a phone OS update. The best first step is

explain: Updates often break companion links; re-pairing and restoring permissions fixes most sync failures.

explain: Geofencing triggers compliance actions, such as disabling the camera on-site or wiping a device that leaves an area.

q: Apple Automated Device Enrollment (ADE) and Android zero-touch enrollment share which benefit?
options: They remove the need for user accounts
Devices configure themselves with management at first setup, straight from the box
They install retail apps for free
explain: Zero-touch/ADE enrollment binds devices to the organization so MDM profiles apply during initial setup.

q: A supervised iOS device allows an organization to
options: Apply restrictions unavailable on unsupervised devices, such as blocking AirDrop
Remove the passcode remotely without a wipe
Install apps without an Apple ID ever
explain: Supervision unlocks deeper management restrictions for organization-owned devices.

q: Factory Reset Protection (FRP) on Android and Activation Lock on iOS both serve to
options: Make a stolen device unusable by requiring the original account after a reset
explain: FRP/Activation Lock bind the device to the prior account, deterring theft and resale.

q: A mobile device management (MDM) solution differs from mobile application management (MAM) in that MAM
options: Manages apps and their data without controlling the whole device
explain: MAM targets corporate apps and data, which suits BYOD where full device control is inappropriate.

q: A phone shows 'No Service' after a drop, but Wi-Fi works. The hardware MOST likely affected is
options: An antenna connection or the SIM seating
explain: Drops can unseat the SIM or disconnect antenna leads, killing cellular while Wi-Fi may use a separate path (though often shared, the SIM/antenna check comes first).

q: Liquid contact indicators inside a phone turning red tell the technician
options: The device has been exposed to liquid, which may affect warranty coverage
explain: LCIs change color on liquid exposure; manufacturers use them when evaluating warranty claims.

q: A mobile screen shows ghost images of the status bar permanently. This is
explain: Static elements displayed for long periods cause uneven OLED wear that appears as persistent ghost images.

q: Before shipping a phone for repair, the user should be told to
options: Ship the phone with the charger only
Back up data and remove or disable account locks per the repair policy
explain: Repairs may erase the device, and activation locks can block testing; backup and documented lock handling prevent loss.

q: A dual-SIM phone user wants work calls on one line and personal on the other. The configuration needed is
options: Assign the SIMs/eSIMs as separate lines and set defaults per contact or app
Merge both numbers into one SIM
explain: Dual-SIM devices let each line have its own number; users set which line is default for calls, data, and contacts.

q: A tablet used as a point-of-sale terminal should be enrolled in MDM with which mode to lock it to the register app?
explain: Kiosk mode pins the device to the POS app, blocking settings and other apps for a dedicated-purpose terminal.

q: Carrier settings updates on a phone primarily deliver
options: Network configuration changes from the carrier (roaming, VoLTE, APN defaults)
explain: Carrier bundles update how the radio talks to the network, independent of full OS updates.

q: A PC reboots randomly under heavy load with no blue screen or error. Temperatures are normal. The MOST likely failing component is
explain: Instant reboots under load with normal temps point to a PSU that cannot sustain the load or is failing; OS crashes usually log errors or blue screens.

q: After installing a new graphics card, the monitor shows no signal, but the PC works on integrated graphics. The FIRST thing to check is
options: That the display cable is plugged into the graphics card, not the motherboard port
explain: The classic mistake: the cable stays in the onboard port, which is disabled or ignored once a discrete GPU is installed.

q: A hard drive makes repetitive clicking noises and has become very slow. The technician should
options: Power it down and treat it as a mechanical failure; further use worsens data loss
Run CHKDSK to repair the heads
explain: The 'click of death' indicates head/actuator failure. Continued operation can destroy the platter surface and the data.

q: A user sets a resolution the monitor cannot handle and now sees 'Input Not Supported.' To recover, the technician should
options: Boot into Safe Mode or use the low-resolution option and set a supported resolution
explain: Safe Mode loads a basic display driver at a safe resolution so the setting can be corrected.

q: On a laptop, the internal screen is black but a very faint image is visible when shining a flashlight at it. The likely failure is
explain: A faint image means the panel is drawing the picture but the backlight (LED/inverter) is not illuminating it.

q: A laser printer leaves a repeating black streak down every page. The most likely culprits are
options: A damaged drum or a dirty/damaged fuser roller
explain: Repeating defects at drum/fuser intervals indicate physical damage or toner buildup on the drum or fuser.

q: An inkjet printer outputs pages with evenly spaced horizontal white lines. The first remedy is
options: Run the printhead cleaning cycle and a nozzle check
explain: White bands across prints are classic clogged nozzles; the built-in cleaning utility usually clears them.

q: One workstation prints garbled characters to a shared printer while everyone else prints fine. The problem is most likely
options: A corrupt or incorrect print driver on that workstation
explain: When only one client garbles output, its driver (or driver version) is mismatched to the printer's language.

q: After someone plugged both ends of a spare patch cable into wall jacks, the whole floor's network collapsed. This created
options: A switching loop flooding the network with broadcast traffic
explain: Connecting two switch ports together loops broadcasts endlessly; STP should prevent it but unmanaged segments still melt down.

q: A desktop negotiates only 100 Mbps on a gigabit port with a known-good switch. Swapping the PC changes nothing. The likely cause is
options: The PC's NIC driver is outdated
One damaged pair in the cable run; gigabit needs all four pairs
explain: 100 Mbps needs two pairs; gigabit Ethernet needs all four. A single bad pair drops the link to 100.

q: An access point reboots several times a day. It is powered by PoE from a switch running many phones and cameras. The likely cause is
options: The channel is set to auto
The switch's PoE power budget is exceeded
explain: When total PoE draw exceeds the switch's budget, devices at the margin reboot under load spikes.

q: A domain user suddenly cannot log in anywhere; the error mentions the computer account or time. The workstation clock is 12 minutes fast. The fix is
options: Reset the user's password five times
Resynchronize the workstation's time with the domain
explain: Kerberos tolerates about five minutes of skew; excessive clock drift breaks domain authentication.

q: Remote VPN users report that large file transfers stall while small pings work after an ISP change. This pattern suggests
options: An MTU mismatch black-holing large packets
explain: When small packets pass but large ones vanish, fragmentation/MTU along the new path is the classic cause.

q: A fiber link between two buildings went down after a storm. Both switches are up. The first checks are
options: Change the VLAN on every port
Reseat the SFPs, inspect for a damaged or sharply bent fiber, and verify strand polarity
explain: Storm damage and disturbed patching are common; also, duplex fiber with swapped TX/RX strands will not link.

q: A new toner cartridge still shows 'Toner Low' immediately. The first step is
options: Reseat the cartridge and confirm the shipping seal/tape was fully removed
explain: Unremoved seals and poorly seated chip contacts make new cartridges read as empty or missing.

q: Paper jams always occur at the same spot in the paper path. After clearing scraps, the persistent cause is usually
explain: Rollers lose grip with wear and paper dust; cleaning or a roller kit restores reliable feeding.

q: Scans from an MFP's document feeder show a thin vertical line that flatbed scans do not. The fix is
options: Clean the narrow ADF scanner glass strip
explain: Feeder scans pass over a small glass strip; a speck on it streaks the entire page length.

q: A laser printer displays 'Perform Maintenance' after reaching its page count, though print quality is fine. The technician should
options: Reset the counter without installing the kit
Install the maintenance kit (rollers/fuser) and reset the maintenance counter
explain: Maintenance messages are page-count driven; the kit replaces wear parts and the counter must be reset.

q: A printer is reachable by IP and prints from wired PCs, but Wi-Fi users in the same office cannot print to it. The likely cause is
options: The printer is out of toner
The wireless clients are on a different VLAN/subnet without routing to the printer
The wired PCs have newer drivers
explain: If wired works and wireless does not, suspect network segmentation: guest or separate wireless VLANs often cannot reach LAN devices.

q: A laptop charges only when the power cable is held at a specific angle. The fault is
options: A worn DC jack or damaged plug
explain: Angle-dependent charging means a broken solder joint or worn barrel connector making intermittent contact.

q: A PC intermittently blue-screens with WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR. This stop code points to
options: A hardware fault (CPU, power delivery, or PCIe device)
explain: WHEA errors are reported by the Windows Hardware Error Architecture and indicate genuine hardware-level problems.

q: As soon as a particular USB device is plugged in, the PC freezes or shuts off. The device or its cable likely
options: Has a short circuit drawing excessive current
explain: A shorted USB device can trip the port's over-current protection and crash or power down the machine.

q: After adding a second RAM stick, the PC boots but shows only half the expected memory. The first action is
options: Reseat the new module firmly until both clips engage
explain: A partially seated DIMM is the most common cause; reseating fixes most 'missing memory' cases.

q: A BIOS update was interrupted by a power cut and now the PC will not POST. The recovery path is
options: Use the board's BIOS recovery/dual-BIOS or USB flashback feature
explain: Modern boards provide crash-recovery (USB BIOS Flashback, dual BIOS) precisely for interrupted updates.

q: Under gaming load, the screen shows colored artifacts and tearing blocks, and the GPU is near its thermal limit. The likely cause is
options: GPU overheating or failing video memory
explain: Artifacts under load with high temperatures indicate the GPU core or VRAM is overheating or degrading.

q: Several adjacent keys on one side of a laptop keyboard stopped working while an external keyboard works fine. The cause is
options: Damage to the keyboard matrix or its ribbon cable
explain: A regional cluster of dead keys maps to a broken row/column trace or a partly unseated ribbon connector.

q: A projector's image is a trapezoid even though the projector is level. The best correction is
options: Square the projector to the screen and use lens shift before digital keystone
explain: Keystone distortion comes from the projector not being perpendicular to the screen; digital keystone costs resolution.

q: After waking from sleep, a USB-C dock's monitors stay black until the dock is power-cycled. This is typically resolved by
options: Updating the dock firmware and the laptop's Thunderbolt/USB-C drivers
explain: Dock wake failures are a well-known firmware/driver interaction; vendors fix them in dock firmware updates.

q: A point-of-sale receipt printer outputs gibberish characters. The most likely causes are
options: A wrong print driver or a mismatched emulation/baud setting
explain: Gibberish on serial/thermal printers usually means the driver language or serial parameters do not match the printer.

q: A server shows an amber light and one of its two power supply LEDs is off. With redundant PSUs, the technician should
options: Shut the server down immediately for a week
Replace both PSUs at the next maintenance window
Hot-swap the failed PSU module; the server keeps running on the other
Replace both PSUs and the motherboard
explain: Redundant PSUs are designed for live replacement: pull the failed module and slide in a spare.

q: A RAID monitoring alert reports the array is 'degraded.' This means
options: One drive has failed and the array is running without redundancy until it is replaced and rebuilt
The array is at full speed
explain: Degraded = a member drive is gone; the data survives on parity/mirror, but a second failure now loses everything.

q: After a power outage, a NAS responds to ping but none of its file shares are available. The likely state is
options: The volume is running a filesystem check or did not mount; check the NAS console/logs
The NAS needs a new IP from the ISP
explain: After dirty shutdowns, NAS units hold shares offline while checking/repairing volumes.

q: A USB printer randomly disconnects, and the cable run is about 8 meters. The root cause is
options: The PC has too much RAM
The cable exceeds the 5-meter USB 2.0 specification limit
explain: USB 2.0 passive cables are limited to 5m; beyond that, signal integrity fails—use a shorter run, a hub, or an active extension.

q: A headset microphone is not detected when plugged into a laptop's single combo audio jack. The headset has separate mic and headphone plugs. The solution is
options: Use a TRRS splitter (Y-cable) that combines mic and headphone into one combo plug
explain: Combo jacks use the 4-conductor TRRS standard; dual-plug headsets need a splitter to merge mic and audio.

q: A technician cleaned a PC's fans with compressed air without holding the blades; now the PC will not boot. A plausible cause is
options: Overspun fans generated voltage that damaged components (or a connector was blown loose)
A fan connector was blown loose
explain: Spinning fans with air turns them into generators that can back-feed voltage; always hold blades still when dusting.

q: A wall-mounted monitor slowly droops downward on its arm. The monitor is 34-inch ultrawide. The cause is
options: The HDMI cable is pulling it down
The HDMI cable is too short
The arm's weight rating is exceeded by the monitor
explain: Monitor arms are rated by weight; an over-weight display overwhelms the tilt friction and droops.

q: An Ethernet wall jack went dead after the office was re-punched during a rewire. Testing at the jack shows two pairs open. The fault is
options: The switch is out of licenses
A bad punchdown termination at the jack or patch panel
explain: Open pairs after rewiring mean conductors were not seated in the IDC contacts; re-punch and retest.

q: A PC's fans roar and temps climb every afternoon. The office faces west. Inspection shows a thick dust mat on the intake filter and heatsink. The correct action is
options: Clean the intake filters and heatsinks; dust insulation is choking airflow
explain: Dust blankets heatsinks and filters, insulating them; afternoon sun load pushes the marginal cooling over the edge.

q: A desktop's wired connection drops whenever the user rolls their chair over the cable under the desk mat. The permanent fix is
options: Disable the NIC power saving only
Replace the damaged cable and route it through a cable channel or raceway
Move the PC closer to the switch only
explain: Repeated crushing breaks conductors intermittently; replacing and protecting the run fixes the root cause.

q: A user's second monitor flickers only at 144Hz but is stable at 60Hz over the same port. The likely cause is
options: A low-quality or overly long DisplayPort cable that cannot carry the high-refresh signal
The monitor needs a firmware password
explain: High refresh rates stress cable bandwidth; marginal cables drop sync at 144Hz but cope at 60Hz.

q: After a thunderstorm, one PC will not power on at all while others on the same strip work. The strip's breaker is fine. The likely failure is
options: The PSU was damaged by the surge
explain: A PC that is completely dead after a surge, with power present at the strip, points to a blown PSU.

q: A laptop's internal speakers crackle and distort at any volume, but headphones sound perfect. The fault is
options: The internal speaker drivers are damaged or blown
explain: Clean headphone output with distorted speakers isolates the failure to the speakers themselves.

q: A PC boots fine cold but crashes after about 20 minutes, and the CPU heatsink is too hot to touch. After confirming fans spin, the next step is
options: Remove, clean, and repaste the heatsink; old thermal paste has likely dried out
explain: Time-dependent overheating with a scorching heatsink means poor heat transfer from CPU to cooler—classic dried paste.

q: A new SSD is installed in an older laptop and is not detected in BIOS at all. The drive works in another machine. A likely compatibility issue is
options: The laptop's SATA controller mode or an outdated BIOS not recognizing the drive
The SSD is too fast for the screen
The laptop needs more RAM first
The power brick wattage is too high
explain: When the drive proves good elsewhere, check controller settings and BIOS support on the host.

q: A user reports the office printer prints their document twice every time. Other users are unaffected. The likely cause is
options: The number of copies is set to 2 in that user's print preferences or the application
explain: Job-specific duplication lives in the client's settings; the printer's own behavior would affect everyone.

q: A laser printer produces pages that are completely blank from every application. Toner was just replaced. The first check is
options: That the toner cartridge's sealing tape/strip was removed and the cartridge is seated
explain: A forgotten sealing strip blocks toner flow entirely; blank pages from all sources point at the cartridge path.

q: Every page from an inkjet printer has one color missing entirely. The cartridge is full. The likely fault is
options: A clogged or failed printhead for that color
explain: A completely absent color with a full cartridge means ink is not reaching the paper—the printhead nozzles are blocked or dead.

q: A switch's uplink LED is lit but no traffic passes to the rest of the network after a contractor re-patched the rack. A probable cause is
options: The uplink was patched into a port configured for a different VLAN
The cable exceeds the maximum length
The switch port is set to half duplex
explain: A live link with no forwarding after re-patching usually means the cable landed on a port in the wrong VLAN.

q: Employees in one wing report the Wi-Fi signal is strong but throughput is near zero at midday. The AP shows 60 associated clients. The issue is
options: The clients are on the 2.4 GHz band only
Too many clients contending on one access point; add capacity or another AP
explain: Association is not capacity: dozens of active clients share one radio's airtime, collapsing real throughput.

q: A home user upgraded to gigabit internet but speed tests cap near 95 Mbps. Their PC connects through an old Fast Ethernet switch. The bottleneck is
options: The ISP is throttling by default
The 100 Mbps switch between the PC and the router
explain: A Fast Ethernet (100 Mbps) hop caps the whole path at ~95 Mbps real-world throughput.

q: A workstation can reach the internet by IP but not by name after its network adapter was replaced. Other PCs are fine. The misconfiguration is
options: Its DNS server settings are blank or wrong
explain: Name resolution failing on one rebuilt machine means its DNS pointers were not restored.

q: A network printer was moved to a new office and now shows 'offline' for everyone, though it prints its own test page. The likely cause is
options: Its IP address changed (DHCP) while clients still target the old address
The paper is the wrong color
The printer needs a new name
explain: Printers should use static/reserved IPs; after a move, a new DHCP lease breaks the clients' port target.

q: A conference-room PC displays on the projector only when set to duplicate; extended mode shows nothing on the projector. The cause is most likely
options: The HDMI cable is labeled wrong
The projector's input resolution/refresh in extended mode exceeds its support (or it is on the wrong input)
explain: Extended mode negotiates independently per display; unsupported mode settings leave the second display blank.

q: A user's monitor shows a pink/green tint after they swapped cables at their desk. The cable is VGA. The cause is
options: The monitor is in night mode
A bent pin on the VGA connector dropping a color channel
explain: Analog VGA carries colors on separate pins; a bent pin kills or skews one channel, tinting the image.

q: A desktop makes a grinding noise that tracks with disk activity, and SMART reports reallocated sectors climbing. The correct action is
options: Run chkdsk monthly and keep using it
Back up immediately and replace the drive; it is mechanically failing
explain: Grinding plus growing reallocated sectors means active mechanical failure—data first, then replacement.

q: A laptop battery indicator jumps from 40% to 5% within minutes. The battery is two years old. This behavior indicates
options: A worn battery with cells that can no longer hold their rated charge
explain: Sudden percentage cliffs mean cell capacity has collapsed unevenly; calibration may mask it briefly, but the pack is worn out.

q: A technician replaces a laptop screen and now the Wi-Fi signal is extremely weak. The bezel was opened during the repair. The likely mistake is
options: The screen is the wrong resolution
The Wi-Fi antenna leads (which run around the display) were pinched or left disconnected
explain: Laptop antennas route through the display lid; screen work frequently disturbs their coax leads.

q: After a Windows feature update, a desktop's Ethernet adapter disappears from Device Manager entirely. Other adapters (Wi-Fi) show. The first fix to attempt is
options: Reinstall the adapter's driver from the manufacturer's site (the update replaced it with an incompatible one)
explain: Feature updates sometimes install broken NIC drivers; a clean vendor driver restores the adapter.

q: A small office's internet dies every time the microwave in the break room runs. Devices are on the 2.4 GHz band. The fix is
options: Move affected devices/APs to the 5 GHz band, away from microwave interference
explain: Microwave ovens leak energy in the 2.4 GHz band and swamp nearby Wi-Fi; 5 GHz avoids it entirely.

q: An office PC's case fans and lights turn on, but there is no display and no beeps. Removing all but one RAM stick changes nothing; the CPU fan header was found unplugged after recent service. The immediate issue is
options: The monitor is on the wrong input
The CPU is overheating instantly or the board is protecting itself because the CPU fan is disconnected
explain: Many boards refuse to run (or shut down in seconds) without a CPU fan signal; reconnecting it is the first step.

q: A barcode label prints with faded patches in the same spot on every label. The media and ribbon are new. The printhead shows a visible line of damage. The fix is
options: Replace the thermal printhead; dead elements cannot be repaired
explain: Faded bands in a fixed position map to dead heating elements in the printhead—it's a replaceable wear part.

q: A user reports their PC 'loses' its second hard drive intermittently; it reappears after a reboot. The data cable looks aged and loose-fitting. The first action is
options: Replace the SATA data cable and reseat power; intermittent drops are classically cable-related
explain: Drives that vanish and return are very often a marginal SATA cable or power connector, not the drive itself.

q: A VoIP phone sounds robotic and choppy during calls while the PC on the same connection is fine for email. The network shows high jitter at peak hours. The remedy is
options: Enable QoS to prioritize the voice traffic/VLAN
Replace the handset with a louder one
explain: Choppy voice is a jitter/latency symptom; prioritizing voice packets over bulk data restores call quality.

q: A newly built PC powers on for one second then shuts off, repeatedly. The motherboard was installed directly without checking the case. A classic cause is
options: A misplaced standoff shorting the back of the motherboard
explain: An extra standoff touching traces shorts the board; the PSU's protection cuts power instantly in a loop.

q: A user spilled a small amount of coffee into a laptop keyboard. It still works, but several keys are sticky. The best advice is
options: Keep using it; it will dry out fine
Blow it dry with compressed air
Power it off, and have the keyboard replaced/cleaned; liquid damage worsens with time and corrosion
Charge it to check for damage
explain: Liquids corrode contacts progressively; prompt shutdown and service prevent a keyboard issue becoming a board failure.

q: After a technician reset BIOS settings to defaults during another repair, Windows now blue-screens at boot with INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE. The setting that most likely reverted is
options: The SATA controller mode (it reverted from AHCI to a different mode)
explain: Windows was installed with AHCI drivers; if the SATA mode flips to IDE/RAID (or the reverse), the boot device becomes inaccessible until the mode is restored.

q: A printer shared from a Windows PC is unreachable after that PC sleeps. The permanent fix is
options: Set the host PC's power plan to not sleep (or share the printer via its own network connection instead)
Reinstall the printer on every client daily
Wake the PC manually each time forever
explain: A sleeping host takes its shared printer offline; keep the host awake or use a truly network-attached printer.

q: A user complains their new wireless mouse lags and stutters. The receiver is plugged into a USB 3.0 hub next to an external drive. The known interference fix is
options: Move the receiver to a USB 2.0 port or use a short extension to distance it from USB 3.0 devices
explain: USB 3.0 ports and drives emit interference in the 2.4 GHz band that disrupts nearby wireless receivers.

q: A smart TV in the lobby buffers constantly on the guest Wi-Fi while a laptop at the same spot streams fine. The TV only supports 2.4 GHz. The environment has 40 visible 2.4 GHz networks. The problem is
options: The TV needs a firmware password
The guest password is too short
Severe 2.4 GHz congestion that the single-band TV cannot escape
explain: In saturated 2.4 GHz environments, single-band devices suffer most; wired Ethernet or a 5 GHz bridge is the practical fix.

q: A technician sees a PC with Event Viewer full of disk warnings (Event ID 7/51) and occasional freezes during file copies. The priority action is
options: Back up the data, then test and plan replacement of the drive
explain: Repeated controller/disk errors during transfers signal a failing drive or path; protect data before deeper tests.

q: Fiber patch cables were swapped during cleaning and now the link is down, with link lights off on both ends. Tx and Rx strands may be reversed. The check is
options: Verify polarity: each side's transmit must land on the other side's receive
explain: A reversed duplex pair is the most common post-cleaning fiber fault; flipping one connector restores polarity.

q: A user's laptop fan runs constantly and the bottom is hot even at idle on the desktop. Task Manager shows a background updater stuck at high CPU. The category of problem is
options: A runaway software process driving heat and fan noise, not a hardware failure
explain: Constant heat at idle with a pegged process is software-driven; ending/fixing the process restores normal thermals.

q: An impact printer used for multipart forms now prints the top copy clearly but lower copies are unreadable. The ribbon is new. The adjustment is
options: The printhead gap (forms thickness lever) is set too far from the platen for the form's thickness
explain: Impact printing transfers force through the stack; an excessive head gap fades lower copies.

q: A server room's rack-mounted UPS begins beeping with a 'replace battery' indicator during a brief outage and the load drops. The correct interpretation is
options: The servers are drawing too little power
The UPS battery can no longer carry the load; schedule battery replacement
The beeping is a network alert
The UPS needs a firmware password
explain: Dropping the load on battery means the cells are exhausted; the UPS provided no runtime when it mattered.

q: A thin client's monitor shows 'No Signal' after a janitor unplugged the desk to clean. All cables look connected. The thin client's power brick LED is off though plugged into the strip. The strip's switch glows. The likely fault is
options: The power brick has failed or its barrel connector is not fully seated
explain: No power LED at the brick with live strip power isolates the failure to the adapter or its connection.

q: A PC was just upgraded with a faster CPU on the same motherboard. It boots but runs the CPU at a low fixed speed. The likely requirement missed is
options: A BIOS update to fully support the new CPU stepping
explain: Boards often need a BIOS update for newer CPU steppings; without it, the chip may run in a safe low-power mode.

q: A QA team needs to test an installer, then instantly return each test VM to a pristine state before the next run. The feature designed for this is
explain: Snapshots capture a VM's state so it can be reverted to a clean checkpoint in moments—ideal for repeatable testing.

q: A 5.25-inch drive bay in a desktop case is the traditional size for
explain: The 5.25-inch bay is the legacy full-size bay designed for CD/DVD/Blu-ray optical drives.

q: An external GPU (eGPU) enclosure gives a laptop desktop-class graphics performance by
options: Housing a desktop graphics card and connecting over Thunderbolt
explain: eGPU enclosures hold a full desktop GPU and link to the laptop over a high-bandwidth Thunderbolt connection.

q: Compared with a full ATX motherboard, a microATX board typically trades
options: Fewer expansion slots for a smaller footprint
The CPU socket for a soldered chip
All USB ports for serial ports
DDR slots for a second battery
explain: microATX keeps the same mounting standard in a smaller board with fewer PCIe slots, suiting compact builds.

q: A PCIe riser cable is used in a build to
options: Connect two monitors to one port
Add more PCIe lanes to the chipset
Relocate or reorient the graphics card (for example, mounting it vertically)
explain: Riser cables are flexible PCIe extensions that let builders position the GPU away from its slot, commonly for vertical display mounts.

q: Many motherboards include a row of small debug LEDs (CPU, DRAM, VGA, BOOT). During a no-POST failure these LEDs
options: Show which stage of initialization is failing
explain: Debug LEDs light at the stage where POST stalls, pointing the technician at the CPU, memory, graphics, or boot device.

q: A discrete TPM module plugs into a motherboard header to add
options: Hardware-backed key storage and platform attestation for boards without a built-in TPM
explain: Boards with a TPM header accept a discrete TPM chip providing the cryptographic key storage BitLocker and Windows Hello rely on.

q: A phone rated IP68 is certified as
options: Dust-tight and resistant to immersion in water within the manufacturer's limits
explain: IP68 means complete dust protection and submersion resistance under specified conditions; it is not a guarantee against all water damage.

q: A company app catalog provided through MDM lets employees
options: Install any app from the public store free
Share one Apple ID across the company
Install organization-approved apps on demand without using personal store accounts for licensing
explain: Volume-licensed apps distributed through the MDM catalog install under organizational licenses, keeping personal accounts out of it.

q: Cracked back glass on a modern phone is more than cosmetic because it can
options: Disable wireless charging and expose internal components to moisture
explain: The back glass protects the wireless charging coil and seals the chassis; cracks break both the seal and charging alignment.

q: When a phone's hotspot is switched from 2.4 GHz to 5 GHz, connected devices typically get
explain: 5 GHz hotspot bands offer more throughput but attenuate faster through walls and distance than 2.4 GHz.

q: Scan-to-folder from the office MFP stopped working the day after a server update disabled SMBv1. The fix is
options: Reconfigure the MFP to use SMBv2/v3 (or update its firmware to support it)
Re-enable SMBv1 permanently on the server
Give the MFP a public IP
explain: SMBv1 is insecure and routinely disabled by updates; devices must be moved to SMBv2/3 rather than weakening the server.

q: An entire floor's network drops for a few seconds several times a day. The switch's logs show it rebooting; its UPS also feeds a space heater someone plugged in. The root cause is
options: The overloaded UPS dropping power to the switch
explain: UPS units are for IT loads; a heater's draw overloads it and browns out everything attached, including the switch.

q: A projector displays a lamp warning and powers itself off after a few minutes of use. The lamp has 3,900 hours on a 3,000-hour rated life. The correct action is
options: Replace the lamp and reset the lamp timer
explain: Projectors shut down to protect aging lamps past their rated hours; a new lamp plus timer reset is the fix.

q: A newly installed case fan makes a loud buzzing that changes when cables near it are moved. The cause is
options: A cable touching the fan blades
explain: Loose cables sagging into a fan's path produce a buzzing/ticking that shifts as cables move; rerouting and securing them cures it.

q: A content delivery network (CDN) improves a website's performance for global visitors by
options: Caching content on edge servers located near the users
Assigning every visitor a static IP
explain: CDNs serve cached copies from geographically close edge nodes, cutting latency and origin load.

q: A retailer runs 10 cloud servers most of the year and scales to 200 during the holiday rush, then scales back down. This cloud characteristic is
explain: Rapid elasticity is the ability to scale resources out and back in quickly to match demand.
